- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects and overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak for next 3 days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days above 75 then dropping), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 2–3 day moving average of true values.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment-driven momentum; weight sentiment history (last 3–5 days) 30% into forecast adjustment.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; use sentiment polarity to bias forecast toward recent sentiment trend.
